summary:
We developed an interactive 3D educational simulation game designed to teach children the fundamentals of resource management, anticipation, and crisis decision-making.

Moving beyond passive virtual exploration, our platform places young players in charge of a virtual environment monitored through four real-time vital stock gauges: Water, Food, Energy, and Materials. When unexpected disasters strike—such as storms, system failures, or supply shortages—the game triggers dynamic decision scenarios. Players must evaluate clear trade-offs, balance immediate action costs against long-term reserves, and learn from instant pedagogical feedback explaining how their choices impact stock levels.

This project is important because resource stewardship, risk mitigation, and strategic thinking under pressure are essential life skills that often feel too abstract for young learners. By transforming complex inventory and crisis management into an intuitive, consequence-driven gameplay loop, our solution empowers children to understand scarcity, prevent waste, and build real-world resilience through active play.
details:
Our project is an interactive 3D educational simulation game that teaches children the fundamentals of resource stewardship, anticipation, and crisis decision-making. Rather than offering a passive virtual sandbox, the application places young players in command of a living environment governed by a real-time Heads-Up Display (HUD) and a dynamic catastrophe engine.

  • Real-Time Stock Monitoring: Players manage four core resource gauges—Water, Food, Energy, and Materials—scaled from 0 (critical depletion) to 100 (full capacity), with continuous visual indicators of system health.
  • Dynamic Disaster Triggers: At key intervals, unexpected crises—such as severe storms, infrastructure failures, or supply shortages—interrupt normal operations and trigger an interactive decision modal.
  • Trade-Off Decision Matrix: Each crisis presents 2 to 3 clear choices with explicit resource costs and risk profiles, such as spending Materials immediately to reinforce systems versus conserving stocks at the risk of heavier damage.
  • Instant Pedagogical Loop: Every decision immediately updates the stock gauges and displays a concise, child-friendly explanation of why reserves increased or dropped, linking choices directly to outcomes.
  • Win and Loss States: Players win by maintaining balanced reserves across a full cycle of disasters; if any single gauge hits zero, the game triggers an educational debrief explaining how to prevent that bottleneck next time.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Traditional educational tools often struggle to teach abstract concepts like scarcity, risk mitigation, and long-term planning in a way that resonates with children.

  • Cognitive Skill Building: The simulation transforms complex systems thinking, budgeting, and prioritization into tangible visual cause-and-effect loops that children can grasp intuitively.
  • Real-World Resilience: By practicing high-stakes decisions in a safe virtual environment, young learners develop foresight, adaptability, and an understanding of why preparation outperforms reactive panic.
  • Sustainable Mindset: The intended long-term impact is to cultivate resource consciousness early in life, helping children understand conservation, waste prevention, and ecological balance both in-game and in the real world.
  • Classroom and Home Accessibility: Running directly in the browser with zero installation required, the platform gives educators and parents a ready-to-use tool that turns screen time into active strategic learning.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

  • Frontend & 3D Rendering: Built with React, JavaScript/TypeScript, and Three.js / React Three Fiber to render the interactive 3D environment alongside a responsive 2D management overlay.
  • Styling & UI Architecture: Styled with Tailwind CSS to create high-contrast, animated resource gauges, crisis alert modals, and accessible decision cards tailored for young readers.
  • Build & Deployment Toolchain: Bundled with Vite for fast hot-module reloading and deployed on Vercel for instant cross-platform web access.
  • AI-Augmented Development Workflow: Engineered using Google Antigravity and OpenCode to orchestrate modular state logic, rapid UI iteration, and ultra-lean code diffs under strict hackathon time and token constraints.
  • Hardware: Developed, tested, and optimized across desktop PC and tablet (iPad Pro) environments to ensure responsive mouse and touch controls.

How the Project Is Creative

Most educational games for children fall into one of two extremes: open-ended 3D sandboxes with no real consequences, or static multiple-choice quizzes disguised as games. Our project bridges this gap by fusing an immersive 3D world with a simplified, visual strategy-game HUD. Furthermore, instead of treating a depleted gauge as a punishing "Game Over," our design reframes failure as an interactive diagnostic moment—showing the child the exact chain of events that led to the shortage so they can immediately test a better strategy.

Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Child UX and Cognitive Load: We avoided dense text and complex numbers, relying instead on color-coded bars, clear iconography, and short, actionable prompts so children never feel overwhelmed during a crisis alert.
  • Pedagogical Balancing: We carefully tuned the resource consumption rates and disaster penalties so that reckless spending and extreme hoarding both carry clear downsides, rewarding balanced, proactive management.
  • Performance and Modularity: To keep the 3D environment running smoothly on standard school tablets and laptops, we decoupled the React state-management crisis loop from the 3D rendering pipeline.
  • Development Efficiency: Operating under tight hackathon deadlines and strict AI compute quotas, we prioritized a clean, surgical architecture that delivered a complete, playable pedagogical loop without bloated dependencies.
